title: FluentWork WSS binary audio frames
description: Byte layout of the WebSocket binary messages on the voice-gateway <-> client socket. The control frames that sit next to this file are JSON and therefore have a JSON Schema; the audio frames are raw bytes and have none. This file is the source of truth for them, and it is frozen by sha256 (see scripts/check-schema-freeze.sh) so that a change to it is deliberate rather than silent.

why_this_file_exists.problem: Before this file the layout existed only as prose in two implementation comments, plus a $defs entry that nothing referenced. Nothing could go red when the two implementations diverged.
measured_evidence: fluentwork-backend internal/voiceproto/frames.go — AITTSAudio.Encode writes a 4-byte big-endian seq followed by the payload
fluentwork-infra schemas/transport/wss-control-frames-v2.json — aiTTSAudio is defined but deliberately absent from oneOf, so the v1/v2 version strategy does not cover this layout
why_this_file_exists.why_now: Stage 3 adds turn_ref to the downlink header. That turns 'two implementation points' into 'two layouts x two repositories = four'. The source of truth lands first so the change has something to be checked against.

conventions.text_frames_are_out_of_scope: JSON control frames are described by wss-control-frames-v2.json

h4.description: Current downlink layout. The frame carries no turn attribution.

h8.status: implemented by both sides; not yet verified end-to-end on a device
h8.description: Downlink layout used once the gateway sets turn_ref on ai.tts.start.

uplink.description: Client audio carries no header at all: the whole WebSocket message is the payload.

rule.when: the most recent ai.tts.start on this socket carries turn_ref
the most recent ai.tts.start on this socket does not carry turn_ref

layout_selection.scope: Until the next ai.tts.start on the same socket.
layout_selection.why_the_switch_is_a_field_and_not_a_vers: A layout switch carried on an existing control frame is what makes a rollback possible without reviving a handshake: the gateway stops setting turn_ref and the client falls back to h4 on its own. A version number would require both ends to agree out of band, which is lockstep, and lockstep has no rollback.

seq.numbering_domain: session — the whole WebSocket, not a turn and not a provider connection
seq.monotonic: strictly increasing for as long as the socket is open
seq.zero_means: unset; the gateway never sends 0, which is reserved because the client's codec uses it to mean unset
seq.purpose: identity for the client's barge-in gate, which drops every frame at or below interrupt.max_seq
seq.implementation_note: One allocator per socket (backend internal/voicegateway/seq_allocator.go). It is handed to a provider at Open rather than owned by one, so a transparent provider reopen cannot restart the numbering behind a watermark already in the hundreds.

turn_ref.numbering_domain: session — same domain as seq, but a separate allocator
turn_ref.monotonic: strictly increasing for as long as the socket is open
turn_ref.purpose: attributes an audio frame to the turn that produced it, so a client can drop a superseded turn's frames after a barge-in instead of relying on its own guess at which turn is current
turn_ref.why_not_the_seq_allocator: seq counts frames and turn_ref counts turns. Sharing one allocator would make seq skip numbers, and seq is the basis of the barge-in watermark.
turn_ref.presence: h8 only. In h4 there is no turn_ref field on the wire at all.

payload.downlink_codec: declared by the codec field of the ai.tts.start that selected the layout
payload.uplink_codec: declared out of band by gateway config VOICE_GATEWAY_CLIENT_AUDIO_FORMAT (opus-framed | pcm-s16le); the client does not negotiate it on the wire
payload.measured_production_value: on the volc-duplex provider path the gateway emits codec 'pcm' at sample_rate 16000, and the client's wired decoder is RawPCM16FrameDecoder, which returns the payload unchanged

invariants.statement: A downlink h4 message is at least 5 bytes.
Bytes 0..4 are seq as a big-endian uint32.
Bytes 4.. are the payload, and it is non-empty.
A downlink h8 message is at least 9 bytes.
Bytes 0..4 are seq as a big-endian uint32.
Bytes 4..8 are turn_ref as a big-endian uint32.
Bytes 8.. are the payload, and it is non-empty.
An uplink message has no header: the whole message is the payload.

invariants.check: for downlink messages i < j on one socket: seq_i < seq_j
invariants.statement: seq strictly increases within one socket and never repeats.

invariants.check: for h8 messages i < j on one socket that belong to different turns: turn_ref_i < turn_ref_j
invariants.statement: turn_ref never repeats across turns and strictly increases from one turn to the next. Every frame of a turn carries that turn's value, so across the message sequence it is non-decreasing rather than strictly increasing — the frame-level reading is unsatisfiable for any turn longer than one frame.

invariants.check: neither side reads the layout from the message length or from the payload's first bytes
invariants.statement: The layout is whatever layout_selection says, and nothing else.
invariants.why: A length heuristic would misread a short h8 frame as h4 and shift the payload by four bytes. That is audible as one click per frame, not as silence — which makes it the harder failure to notice.

uplink_chunk_bytes.meaning: 20 ms of 16 kHz mono PCM16 (320 samples). The client sends one WebSocket binary message per chunk.
uplink_chunk_bytes.status: convention, not enforced by this layout
uplink_chunk_bytes.drift_note: Two constants hold this value: backend internal/voicegateway/uplink_constants.go UplinkChunkBytes and internal/voiceduplex/volc_duplex.go uplinkChunkBytes. Equal today; changing one does not redden the other.

known_divergences.summary: Three places still describe the downlink payload as Opus; a fourth — the description of the retired wss-control-frames-v1.json — went with that file. The implementation that actually runs treats the payload as raw PCM16, and the gateway declares codec 'pcm'.
claims_saying_opus: fluentwork-ios Shared/FluentWorkNetworking/Socket/WSAudioFrameCodec.swift:5-6 — 'The payload is whatever the active ai.tts.start codec says it is — Opus in the gateway's current shape, already-PCM16 under RawPCM16FrameDecoder.'
fluentwork-ios Shared/FluentWorkCore/Dependencies/AppDependencies.swift — VolcengineOpusFrameDecoder doc: 'iOS never receives Opus data in production'
fluentwork-meta docs/30_技术方案/30_FluentWork技术方案设计文档.md:72 — '音频帧：Opus 编码，20ms 帧'
known_divergences.claims_citation_note: Citations refreshed 2026-09-26. The iOS entry used to cite the `Binary layout: ... + Opus payload bytes` comment, which Stage 3 rewrote to describe h4 and h8 instead, so that comment is no longer one of these claims; the surviving iOS claim is the one cited now. Line numbers here drift — the quoted text is the identity.
evidence_saying_pcm: fluentwork-ios Shared/FluentWorkCore/Dependencies/AppDependencies.swift — the wired decoder is RawPCM16FrameDecoder, whose decode() returns the payload unchanged and only rejects an odd byte count
fluentwork-ios Shared/FluentWorkCore/Dependencies/AppDependencies.swift — VolcengineOpusFrameDecoder.decode throws notAvailable and is not bound
fluentwork-backend internal/voicegateway/provider_volc_duplex.go — ai.tts.start is emitted with codec 'pcm' and sample_rate 16000
known_divergences.consequence: The codec is not named anywhere on the wire except ai.tts.start.codec, so nothing goes red. A reader following the prose would build an Opus decoder for data that is already PCM16.
known_divergences.resolution: Not decided here. This artifact records the measured value and stays codec-agnostic by design; the three prose claims are for their own repositories to correct or justify.

known_divergences.summary: wss-control-frames-v2.json defines aiTTSAudio but deliberately omits it from oneOf, so the v1/v2 version strategy never applied to the binary layout. Before this file, no artifact owned it.
known_divergences.resolution: This file owns it. Layout changes are made here, and the digest in scripts/check-schema-freeze.sh is refreshed deliberately — never to smuggle a field in.
